name: Green (Sirun) Wang
bio: I am an undergraduate at UC Berkeley studying political economy and applied mathematics. I am interested in how institutions and information shape what people value and believe, particularly how preferences and beliefs develop together in different institutional settings.
approach: My current questions concern the formation of preferences and beliefs. I hope to use formal models to explore their interaction, starting from historically specified conditions and examining how different paths may unfold. I am also interested in how ways of measuring and comparing value affect both behavior and our interpretation of historical evidence.
researchLead: How do institutions shape what people value and believe?
currentFocus: How preferences and beliefs develop within institutions.
contactTopics: preference formation, institutions, and formal political economy
bioZh: 我目前是加州大学伯克利分校的本科生，学习政治经济与应用数学。我对制度与信息如何影响人们的评价和信念感兴趣，尤其希望理解偏好与信念如何在不同制度环境中共同形成。
approachZh: 我目前关注偏好与信念的形成，希望学习用形式模型研究两者的相互作用，从具体历史条件出发，考察可能出现的不同演化路径。我也关心衡量和比较价值的方式如何影响行为，以及我们对历史材料的理解。

workingHypothesis.title: Monetary valuation and preferences
workingHypothesis.status: Exploratory interest; not a finding or a confirmed course-paper topic
workingHypothesis.question: Can expressing different forms of value in monetary terms change what people come to value?
workingHypothesis.note: I would like to explore this question in the context of capitalist institutions. The relationship between monetary valuation and preference formation is a starting point for further study.
